title: Panel B, Panel B, Panel B
subject: a man in a Swindon back garden assembling a flat-pack shed on a Saturday and finding the kit has three wall panels stamped B and none stamped C, so he builds it anyway with the window facing the fence
caption: Skiffle revival, 1950s British skiffle party style. Fast strummed acoustic guitar on boom-chick rhythm, scratched washboard with thimbles, thumping tea-chest bass, wailing harmonica fills between lines. Dry live front-room recording, close mics, small room. Male tenor, clearly sung melody, bright music-hall phrasing with group shouts on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 168 BPM, G major. Cheerful, flustered, grinning. No electric guitars, no drum kit, no synths, no autotune, no modern pop production.
lyrics:
[Intro - washboard, strummed guitar]

[Verse 1]
Saturday morning, the van's been and gone
Forty-two pieces and one little spanner
I laid them all out on the lawn in a row
And the instructions are written in Swedish

[Pre-Chorus]
I looked for C and I looked again
All I found was B, B, B

[Chorus]
Panel B, panel B, panel B
Where's the panel that they owe to me
I'll screw it together, I'll make it agree
With panel B, panel B, panel B

[Verse 2]
The roof's on now and it's leaning a bit
The door opens inward and hits the mower
The window's lovely, a proper bay
And it looks straight out at the fence

[Pre-Chorus]
My wife came out with a mug of tea
She said love, is that meant to be

[Chorus]
Panel B, panel B, panel B
Nobody's sending a panel C
I'm calling it finished, it's standing for me
On panel B, panel B, panel B

[Outro - harmonica, last washboard roll]
Three panel B's and a view of the fence
